card.statement:
Note that the universal quantization $\mathcal{A}$ is constructed from the commutative $\mathcal{O}(X)$ in two steps: (i) one first takes the universal deformation $\mathcal{X}$ of $X$, whose deformation base is $H^{2}(X)$, and (ii) one takes the $k[\![\hbar]\!]$ -linear quantization of $\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{X})$. These are reflected in the introduction of (i) $T^{!}$ -equivariant parameters $H^{2}_{T^{!}}(\mathrm{pt})\cong(\mathfrak{t}^{!})^{*}$ and the (ii) $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -equivariant parameter $H^{2}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}(\mathrm{pt})\cong k\hbar$ on the dual side, respectively. ∎

The quantum Hikita conjecture introduced by [KMP21, Conjecture 5.1] extends the Hikita–Nakajima conjecture further to include the data of roots and $D$ -modules.

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
